laws.rule: Vorarlberg has no single Land tax rate. Each council may charge a guest tax (Gästetaxe) set in its own tax order (Taxordnung), under sections 13 to 17 of the Tourismusgesetz. The law caps it at EUR 3.80 per night, a figure from 2015 that is indexed each year (section 16(3); about A$6.04 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026, before indexing; the current cap was not read). Everyone who stays overnight pays (section 14). Exempt (section 15): children under 14, school students away from home, stays of three months or more, hospital patients, people on a work stay of three weeks or more, and those in a second home that pays the second-home levy. It falls due on the last day, and the host collects it (section 17).
laws.heading: Tourismusgesetz, sections 13 to 17

laws.rule: In Vorarlberg the mayor must ban putting up tents, caravans and similar movable shelters outside campsites by order (Bescheid) where safety, health, the local community, farming, tourism, nature or the landscape would be badly harmed (section 14(1) of the Campingplatzgesetz). A council can also pass a regulation allowing it only in set places, or barring it in set places (section 14(2)). Putting one up despite a ban or such a regulation is an offence with a fine of up to EUR 700 (about A$1,112 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026; section 19(1)(g) and (2)). Ask the council for the local regulation.
laws.heading: Campingplatzgesetz, sections 14 and 19

laws.rule: Vorarlberg's Kinder- und Jugendgesetz bars giving alcohol to children and young people under 16, and, at any age under 18, giving them spirits (drinks with distilled alcohol) or serving anyone who is clearly drunk (section 16(2)). The same law bars children and young people from buying, having or using tobacco products, related products and their devices (section 16(3)(a)).
laws.heading: Kinder- und Jugendgesetz, section 16

laws.rule: Vorarlberg curfew for minors in public places: children may not be in public places from 23:00 to 05:00, and young people up to the end of their 16th year not from 01:00 to 05:00, unless with a supervising person or for a serious reason (section 12 of the Kinder- und Jugendgesetz).
laws.heading: Kinder- und Jugendgesetz, section 12

items.text: Vorarlberg's youth-protection law (Kinder- und Jugendgesetz, section 16): under 16, no alcohol; from 16 to 18, beer and wine are allowed, but not spirits. Alcohol may also not be supplied to a young person who is already obviously intoxicated. Offences of acquiring, possessing or consuming alcohol under this law are punished only if they are committed in public (section 21(2)). Youth protection does not apply to a person serving in the Bundesheer or Zivildienst. Children are under 14; youth are 14 to 18. Fines: an adult up to EUR 5,000 (about A$7,945); a young person, a talk or community service and then a fine of up to EUR 500 (about A$795).

psychoactive-substances.notes: These are Land youth-protection rules, not a general adult drinking age of 18 for beer or wine. They apply to visitors under 18 in this Land. Federal narcotics law is not restated here. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293. Official RIS consolidated text (Geltende Fassung) read directly on 11 November 2026.
